newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian rupee slips to close at 35.92/94 per dollar.
newsitem.headline: Indian rupee slips to close at 35.92/94 per dollar.

text.p: The Indian rupee slipped to 35.927/947 against the dollar at the close of trading on Thursday following the entry of a Calcutta bank, dealers said.
The dollar had opened the day at 35.86/88 per dollar and did not see much movement until half an hour before the close.
"It was quiet and dull for the major part of the day with only stray deals," said a dealer. "He came towards the close and hit most Bombay banks," he said, referring to the Calcutta bank.
Dealers said the rupee was moving as expected.
"It was expected to breach 35.90-mark in December," said a dealer. He said most participants had discounted the prediction of the rupee touching the 36 per dollar mark in January 1997.
"His reserves are in very good shape but the country is in a bad shape," another dealer said, referring to Reserve Bank of India's foreign currency assets of over $19.0 billion.
But a deceleration in India's exports and imports did not augur well for the country, the dealer said.
The deceleration in imports was more worrying as it represented a fall in purchases of capital goods and raw materials, pointing to a slowdown in the economy, dealers said.

Exports fell to $2.48 billion in November compared to $2.58 billion during the year ago period, according to government figures. Imports fell to $2.95 billion in November compared to $3.10 billion in last November.
A dealer at a French bank's Bombay office said the exchange rate could play a major role in export promotion.
Most dealers expect a 5.0-7.0 percent depreciation in the rupee's rate in 1997, more or less in line with inflation differentials.
